spec: METHODOLOGY §2.5, §6 — Full Run 2: first run with the mechanical roster rule applied and snapshotted (D-007 item 9), plus the §2.5 as-deployed arm and the §0 retrieval-delta arm (scopes in DEVIATIONS D-008). R1's roster file is preserved at runs/R1/models.json.

roster_rule.rule: For each covered vendor (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google — the R1 set): every generally-available model in the vendor's current top model family at the snapshot date, enumerated mechanically from the vendor's models API where one exists, excluding specialist ids (codex/search/tts/image/embedding/audio), '-lite' ultralight tiers, '-chat-latest' aliases (they float, breaking reproducibility), dated snapshot duplicates of an included base id, and preview/codename models (no dated GA snapshot); PLUS any prior-wave model still callable, carried for cross-wave comparability and flagged. Access gaps between the public lineup and what this project's keys can call are logged as deviations, never silently absorbed.
roster_rule.anthropic_snapshot: Current deployed lineup: Claude 5 family (claude-fable-5, claude-opus-5, claude-sonnet-5) + claude-haiku-4-5 — 4 models, unchanged from R1.
roster_rule.openai_snapshot: GET /v1/models on 2026-08-05: highest GA family with dated snapshots = gpt-5.5 (gpt-5.5-2026-04-23) -> gpt-5.5, gpt-5.5-pro. gpt-5.6-luna/sol/terra excluded as codename previews (no dated snapshots). Superseded-family light tiers (gpt-5.4-mini/nano) excluded by the top-family rule; noted, not hidden: OpenAI currently markets no 5.5-tier mini/nano.
roster_rule.google_snapshot: ListModels on 2026-08-05: highest GA (non-preview) family callable = Gemini 2.5 -> gemini-2.5-pro, gemini-2.5-flash (gemini-2.5-flash-lite excluded as '-lite'). gemini-3-* and 3.1-* are all '-preview'. gemini-3-flash-preview carried from R1 (prior-wave comparability), flagged preview. NOTE the access change since R1: this key could call NO GA Gemini model on 2026-07-28; it can now — the R1 single-preview-model asymmetry (ADDENDA §4) is closed.

arms.uniform: The §2.5 uniform minimum-reasoning protocol arm — the headline. Settings per roster entry below.
arms.deployed: The §2.5 as-deployed arm (vendor defaults). Materially distinct ONLY for the OpenAI models (reasoning_effort omitted instead of pinned to minimum). For the Claude arm the harness exposes no settings, so uniform == as-deployed by construction; for the Gemini arm the uniform arm already sends no overrides, so uniform == as-deployed. Both coincidences are disclosed here and in the report rather than double-run to fabricate an arm. Run as sibling run id R2D sharing R2's frozen bank and snapshots.
arms.retrieval: The §0 retrieval-delta arm — vendor-native retrieval only, never StatCite (the committed retrieval prompt bans StatCite by name). Scope pre-registered in D-008: a seeded 30-question stratified subset of the R2 headline, one flagship per vendor chosen mechanically (highest R1 uniform WTR per vendor: claude-opus-5, gpt-5.5, gemini-3-flash-preview), run as sibling run id R2V. Claude via a Claude Code subagent with web search permitted; OpenAI via the Responses API web_search tool; Google via the google_search grounding tool.

settings_notes: Batching retained at 10 questions per call with the §2.3 controls. §2.3's pre-committed intent to move to single-question calls 'if budget allows' is again not exercised: ~9 models x ~137 questions x up to 3 arms at single-question granularity is outside this run's budget; logged in D-008 rather than silently dropped.
The seed is a pre-announced NIST Randomness Beacon 2.0 pulse (questions/R2-seed-announcement.json), fulfilling §6's Wave-1 seeding commitment; the announcement commit precedes the pulse's existence.

The §6 contamination protocol runs for the first time: 40-question frozen core panel selected mechanically from R1's bank (questions/R2-core.json, seeded by the beacon master seed), fresh majority draw for the remaining 60; the core-vs-fresh gap is published in the report.

Null probes: 25 (§3.4 first-full-wave floor). Reweighting weights frozen pre-call (snapshots/R2/weights.json). Year-discrimination dual metric reported per ADDENDA §3. Parse-policy sensitivity produced by tools/parse_sensitivity.mjs as a standard output.

Publication sequencing: R2 results are NOT pushed to the public repo or statcite.com until covered vendors have received the §8 courtesy preview and 5 business days have elapsed — the reverse of R1's D-004 breach. Pre-registration artifacts (this file, the bank, snapshots, amendments) are public before model calls; results are held locally through the preview window.
